Hi Elena — great question, thanks for flagging. Short answers up front, followed by a couple of concrete examples.

1) Top-up slabs vs per-minute: We offer two burst billing modes for Dedicated customers:
   - Slab Top-ups (recommended for predictable, episodic bursts): you buy blocks of GPU-minutes (e.g., 250 / 500 / 1,000) at a discounted surge rate. Consumption draws down the slab until it’s exhausted; further bursts roll to per-minute billing.
   - Per-minute surcharge (recommended for very spiky, unpredictable bursts): bursts are metered minute-by-minute at a published surcharge (x% over base reserved rate). No upfront slab purchase required.

2) Cooldowns & repeated exceedances: we have a configurable cooldown window (default 6 hours) to limit continuous burst ramping for a single tenant. If usage pattern indicates sustained bursting beyond N cooldown windows in a rolling 30-day period, we’ll propose either: (a) moving you to a higher reserved commit, or (b) applying a usage-tier surcharge for the remainder of the billing cycle. We do not apply punitive "penalties" per se without prior notice — the standard workflow is: alert -> recommended plan change -> customer approval.

Example scenarios (quick numbers):
- Reserved: 16-GPU pool, baseline throughput 14k tokens/sec. Burst slab: 500 GPU-minutes @ 0.45x base price. Per-minute surcharge: 1.6x base.
- If you consume 350 GPU-minutes of bursts/month, slab saves ~28% vs per-minute. If you spike above 500, the first 500 draw from slab, remainder billed per-minute.

Cc’ing Laura (Sales Lead) and Aditya (Solutions Eng) to confirm discounts for a multi-quarter commit and to size the recommended slab for your workload. I’ll follow up with a short proposal and a capacity estimate spreadsheet.

Would you like the slab example modeled against your nightly batch profile? If yes, can you share a sample hour-by-hour load for one week (CSV/P95 of jobs)?

Thanks,

Laura / Aditya,

Forwarding the Quantify thread — they’re leaning toward a 12–18 month reserved commit for a 16-GPU Dedicated pool but are worried about nightly batch-driven bursts ~3–4x baseline for 20–40 minutes, 3x/week. They asked specifically whether to buy a 500 GPU-minute slab or stay on per-minute billing.

My suggested commercial approach:
- Offer a 12-month commit at 85% of list reserved rate (standard for this ARR band).
- Include a 500 GPU-minute burst slab at 0.5x base per-minute equivalent (i.e., slab is cheaper than per-minute surcharge).
- If they exceed the slab >2 times per week for more than 3 weeks in a rolling 30-day window, trigger an automated recommendation to increase to a 20-GPU pool with proportional commit, with a 30-day review window.
- For one-time overages beyond slab in the initial months, bill at per-minute surcharge (1.6x) — but provide a one-time "goodwill" credit equal to 10% of the overage if they commit to the 12-month term within 14 days.

Questions for you: what discount flexibility do we have if they push for 75% reserved rate? Also confirm if legal needs a special clause for the cooldown -> recommendation workflow (we typically avoid hard penalties).

Thanks — Priyom

Subject: Proposed top-up structure & next steps (Quantify.AI)

Hi Elena / Carlos — thanks for the patience while we pulled numbers together. Attached: a short capacity estimate (QuantifyAICapacityEstimate.xlsx) and a draft term sheet with the top-up options called out (Draft-Topup-Terms-2026-10-02.pdf). Summary below.

Proposal (high level):
- Reserved commit: 12-month, 16-GPU pool at 85% of list reserved rate (annual billing).
- Burst add-on Option A (Slab): 500 GPU-minutes top-up slab at 0.5x base per-minute equivalent. Slab runs down first; overage billed at per-minute surcharge (1.6x).
- Burst add-on Option B (On-demand): No slab; bursts billed per-minute at 1.6x.
- Cooldown & operational policy: default cooldown = 6 hours per instance; if the account records >2 slab-exhaustion events per week for 3 consecutive weeks, our console will recommend increasing the pool to 20 GPUs. We will not automatically upgrade without signed agreement.

Economics & incentive: if Quantify.AI signs the 12-month commit within 14 days, we will: (a) extend reserved-rate to 82% of list (one-time concession) and (b) provide a one-time overage credit equal to 10% of the first month’s slab overage (if any).

Next steps:

- I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync with Aditya to validate latency/throughput targets and finalize the recommended slab.
- If the commercial terms look good, I’ll circulate the term sheet for signature (DocuSign).
